rv.q: No one’s going to rain on Sheridan Smith’s parade: this is the best female performance to be seen in the West End.
What the plot lacks in coherence, Mayer’s production amply supplies in verve and sheer spectacle, with admirably crisp musical direction by Theo Jamieson.

Daresay Fanny Brice had it too. It’s not quite a one-woman show: there’s a fine chorus, strong support from performers such as Marilyn Cutts as Fanny’s briskly loving mother and Joel Montague as Fanny’s lovelorn accompanist.

Sheridan Smith Funny Girl triumphantly reinvents Brice for a new generation of musical theatre lovers, conveying with skill and heart this entertainer's emotive blend of professional success and personal vulnerability.
It's a touching, open performance: a superb star turn in a show that questions what it is that makes a star.

It is comprehensively done and will give plenty of pleasure.
Aside from this, the production provides an enjoyable evening, but not a breath-taking one.
Smith may have made its revival possible but this production hasn't transferred from its Off-West End roots well.

cn.t: Sheridan Smith delivers a triumphant, star-making performance that banishes Streisand comparisons, charming audiences with her hilarious, touching take on Fanny Brice in this acclaimed West End revival.
